description: Participants build the language layer of a customer-service system for a fictional regional water utility whose messages arrive in Modern Standard Arabic, Gulf dialect, Arabic written in Latin script and English. They trace text through tokenisers, embeddings and attention, build semantic search, route messages and extract account fields three ways (a classical baseline, a prompted generative model and a fine-tuned encoder), adapt a model with low-rank adapters in free notebook memory, and ship the chosen model as a small service with a model card. Every choice rests on scores by dialect, latency and cost.
audience: Practitioners. Engineers who have completed the level 200 set or can show equivalent work: a deployed model or language model application they built and can explain.
prerequisites: AE-202 Deep Learning and Generative AI Fundamentals
Trains a small neural network with a hand-written training loop
Computes precision, recall and F1 from predictions
Reads and writes UTF-8 Arabic text in Python

outcomes.text: Explain how tokenisation, embeddings and attention turn Arabic and English text into model inputs, and where script, diacritics and dialect break that pipeline, given 50 parallel messages and three tokenisers
outcomes.evidence: a one-page note with token counts per language and two failures traced to their cause

outcomes.text: Implement semantic search over a bilingual message archive and measure it for each language variety, given 2,000 synthetic messages and 40 labelled queries
outcomes.evidence: a table of recall at 10 for each of the four varieties

outcomes.text: Implement schema-validated extraction of account numbers, districts and complaint types from free text, masking personal fields before text reaches a hosted model, given 200 messages with gold fields
outcomes.evidence: field-level precision and recall, a log of validation failures and a passing masking test

outcomes.text: Apply low-rank adapter fine-tuning to an encoder within a fixed memory budget and compare it with full fine-tuning, given a routing set split by customer and a free notebook GPU
outcomes.evidence: training logs, trainable-parameter counts and test scores for both runs

outcomes.text: Decide among a classical baseline, a prompted generative model and a fine-tuned encoder for message routing, given eight departments, a held-out test set and a latency budget
outcomes.evidence: a table of macro F1, F1 by dialect, CPU latency and cost per thousand messages, with a defended recommendation

outcomes.text: Deliver the chosen model as a tested service with a model card that states its limits by language variety, given a smoke-test set
outcomes.evidence: a running service that passes the smoke test and a model card with results by dialect and a hand-off rule
